item.title: HDFC Bank slips despite Nifty Bank recovery, analysts retain buy ratings
item.description: HDFC Bank fell 2.16 per cent even as banking indices gained, with analysts retaining positive ratings while investors assess the lender's transition under new CEO Anup Bagchi ...
item.dc:creator: Shilpa Rangarajan
item.content:encoded: HDFC Bank pared 2.16 per cent in losses even as the Nifty Bank index and the broader Nifty 50 index showed signs of recovery on Monday, after it appointed Anup Bagchi as its new chief executive officer (CEO) on Thursday. A newly appointed CEO is ideally great news for the stock. Markets look forward to the change. However, in the case of HDFC Bank, while the markets have given an initial thumbs-up to Anup Bagchi, investors prefer to wait and watch as the bank is going through a transition. A Macquarie report says that growth is skewed towards deposits rather than AUM and that its CASA is weak. However, brokers also noted a 33 per cent upside potential for the bank's share price. The country’s largest bank by market capitalisation closed at ₹705.65, even as it had 47 buy ratings and two holds, with a 40.1 per cent return potential, according to Bloomberg data. Over the past week, the bank received 14 “buy” ratings and five “outperform” ratings from 21 brokerage firms. Macquarie’s report said HDFC Bank’s Q2FY27 pre-quarter update showed moderate AUM growth of 15.3 per cent year-on-year (YoY) and 5.8 per cent quarter-on-quarter (QoQ), trailing peers, while deposits rose 18.8 per cent YoY and 4.9 per cent QoQ, boosted by $11.5 billion in FCNR inflows (without which growth would have been around 15 per cent YoY and 1.5 per cent QoQ). The report added that growth remains skewed towards term deposits and CASA is weak, as it averaged 10.7 per cent YoY and 1.5 per cent QoQ (₹971.2 billion in the latest quarter versus ₹957 billion in the previous quarter and ₹877 billion a year ago), while its period-end CASA showed growth of 10.8 per cent YoY and 2.6 per cent QoQ (₹1.052 trillion). The loan-to-deposit ratio eased around 200 basis points YoY but edged up QoQ. Macquarie retained an “outperform” rating (target price of ₹875) and added, “while we believe a turnaround in reported performance and a recovery of lost ground will take time, the incoming CEO may have a clear mandate to reinvigorate loan growth, particularly in the retail portfolio, and reclaim deposit market share, with a sharper focus on rebuilding the CASA franchise.” Meanwhile, Nifty Bank closed 0.48 per cent higher at 54,714.1, and the benchmark Nifty 50 closed 0.6 per cent higher at 22,555.75, while the BSE Bankex closed 0.7 per cent higher at 61,788.52, with the broader BSE Sensex closing 0.66 per cent higher at 61,788.52. The market recovery in the banking indices was anchored by the 1.63 per cent gain in ICICI Bank and the 4.28 per cent gain in AU Bank, even as HDFC Bank and y Bank dragged the banking indices down. “Overall, I think things are looking alright from here on. Since 2025, concerns around governance and leadership had led to a nearly 30% correction in its market price. Now, with Anup Bagchi taking over as CEO, we expect the bank’s performance to improve as he settles in and gets a better grip on the business. The bank continues to have strong ratings and a solid franchise. So, in my view, it is more a question of time before the improvement starts reflecting in the performance,” said Somil Mehta, head of retail research at Mirae Asset Sharekhan.

item.title: Flipkart invests in TravClan to strengthen international travel offerings
item.description: The investment will strengthen international travel supply, on-ground support and holiday offerings for customers across Cleartrip and Flipkart Travel ...
item.dc:creator: Peerzada Abrar
item.content:encoded: E-commerce firm Flipkart has taken a minority stake in TravClan, a global B2B travel tech platform. The investment will strengthen international travel supply and expand the holiday packages available to customers across Cleartrip and Flipkart Travel. The companies didn’t reveal the financial details of the deal. Nishant Verman, SVP, corporate development and partnerships, Flipkart, said investing in TravClan strengthens the company’s ability to offer international holiday packages while deepening travel capabilities. “Travellers today are looking for more than a flight or hotel booking. They want a holiday that is curated around their interests and supported throughout the journey. TravClan’s supplier network and destination capabilities will help us build that experience across Cleartrip and Flipkart Travel,” said Verman. TravClan powers outbound leisure travel with direct supplier listings across domestic and international destinations. Its tech platform enables over 15,000 travel agents to instantly customise and book real-time packages, hotels, and activities, backed by 24/7 on-ground customer support. By integrating TravClan’s partner network, technology and destination operations, Cleartrip and Flipkart Travel can offer customers a wider range of international holiday packages, supported by on-ground assistance. Arun Bagaria, co-founder and CEO, TravClan, said India is becoming one of the largest outbound travel markets in the world, with travellers taking their first international trips driving a significant part of this growth. “The opportunity lies in making these trips more affordable while maintaining reliable service levels. By contracting directly with suppliers and operating our own ground teams, we are able to offer competitive prices and deliver a consistent experience,” said Bagaria. “This partnership with Flipkart allows us to take affordable travel products to millions of Indians as they embark on their international journeys.” The funding will support investment in global supply, technology and destination expansion as TravClan scales its platform and grows its team across business development, engineering and destination operations.

item.title: Former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon to testify at NYC hearing on AI
item.description: Coxon will appear at request of Council Speaker Julie Menin, who has urged AI whistleblowers to testify as city lawmakers weigh a package of bills aimed at establishing safeguards around technology ...
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: By Nacha Cattan and Laura Nahmias Former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon, who warned that artificial intelligence could become too powerful for humans to control, will testify Monday at a New York City Council hearing alongside representatives of some of the world’s biggest AI companies.  Coxon will appear at the request of Council Speaker Julie Menin, who has urged AI whistleblowers to testify as city lawmakers weigh a package of bills aimed at establishing safeguards around the technology, according to people familiar with the matter.  Coxon quit Anthropic last month and issued a stark warning about the race to develop increasingly powerful AI, accusing his former employer and OpenAI of “gambling with our lives.” He confirmed he plans to testify on Monday. The hearing will put some of the industry’s most vocal critics in the same room as representatives of Anthropic, OpenAI, Alphabet Inc.’s Google and Meta Platforms Inc.  Former Google DeepMind researcher Alex Turner and Daniel Kokotajlo, executive director of the AI Futures Project and a former OpenAI researcher, are also expected to testify, according to one of the people. The four major AI companies will send policy and safety officials, the person said.  Turner confirmed he plans to attend the hearing. A spokesperson for Google declined to comment. Kokotajlo and representatives of the other companies didn’t respond to requests for comment. The hearing is part of an effort by New York officials to play a larger role in regulating an industry that has expanded rapidly in the city even as much of AI regulation remains the province of federal and state governments. One proposal before the council, sponsored by Menin, would give whistleblowers a portion of fines or penalties recovered from AI companies following reported violations. Other legislation under consideration would allow people harmed by AI systems to sue developers under certain circumstances and require third-party validation of some systems before they can be deployed in the city. OpenAI, Anthropic and Google agreed to appear after Menin’s office warned that they could be subpoenaed, while Meta had committed to attending earlier, Bloomberg News previously reported. The Council subpoenaed SpaceX’s artificial intelligence unit after it failed to respond to requests to appear.
